rapport_notes: Warm, empathetic tone; strong connection with grieving customer; supportive language ('you got this'), but occasional clarity issues in phrasing.
process_discipline_notes: Rep did not hold silence after 'does that feel fair' equivalent—pivoted immediately; no rate-lock or explicit close ask at the end of call.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: None — rep launches directly into agenda question without time-boxing the ask or promising an accurate quote in return.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked: 'Did you have any just top of mind, questions or concerns that I can just make sure that I tackle right on' — but this came after customer had already mentioned boxes concern, so it was asked after probing began, not before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concern about more boxes than anticipated and fragile items (antique radio, plants). Rep acknowledged but did not probe deeply: 'Okay.' 'Okay, gotcha.' One-line acknowledgments, no 'tell me more' or 'what else' follow-up to unpack the real pain. Customer did self-manage some follow-up ('I'm gonna try to pack it up myself'), but rep did not drive the second layer.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Rep said: 'So we do have our on know where we damage coverage which covers up to $2,000 worth of incidental... outside of the 60¢ per pound.' Answered in Stage 1 as direct response to customer's implied carefulness concern (antique radio, fragile items).
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Rep said: 'So the movers that come to you, they will be professionally trained and that it... we don't work with con, daily contract at workers.' Answered in Stage 1 when customer asked if movers are bonded.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Never mentioned. Customer raised traffic concern ('I was hoping we could beat the traffic. That's, that was my concern'), but rep addressed it with prep advice, not with an On-Time Guarantee.
evidence_quotes.communication: Never mentioned. No day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates discussed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor_and_adjust: Rep said: 'So just kind of ballpark it. What would you say that looks like?' and later 'The average is about 45 to 55 boxes for 1200 square foot. So, yeah. So that's average.' Then: 'I am going to move this, I'm gonna add another another two hours to this move... seven and a half to eight and a half is kind of what I'm estimating.' Range given (7.5–8.5 hrs) and light personalization to square footage and drive time, but not a strong anchor-and-adjust frame.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Rep said: 'The great thing is if it ends up not taking that long Lanta then you'll only pay for the time you use. So if we do get around that six, oh, yeah, if we do get around that 67 hours, that's all you end up paying for anyway.'
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Rep said: 'Any kind of miscellaneous items that you may have... any kind of small like just miscellaneous things if everything is just boxed up in some way then, and they're just able to get in there and just they're just wrapping pad in the furniture and moving the boxes out that tremendously helps... if they don't have to put things in boxes.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: Rep said: 'If it ends up not taking that long Lanta then you'll only pay for the time you use' — implies the estimate is flexible, but does not explicitly state 'the estimate is a window because your move is yours' with specific factors named.
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock ('your rate locks when you book') or explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?'). Call ends with: 'My name is Shany and if you need anything in the meantime, you just let us know, okay.' and 'Bye-bye.' — warm but no close.

top_strength: Exceptional warmth and emotional intelligence—Chauntelle met a grieving customer with genuine compassion, acknowledged the difficulty of the estate process, and sustained rapport throughout without being dismissive or transactional.
coaching_note: Lead with quid pro quo framing before any probing, ask the agenda question *before* logistics, and follow up two layers deep on every concern raised; on Stage 3, deliver the full Save Your Ass sequence (all 5 lines) and close with an explicit ask and rate-lock statement.
